notes.title: Concept - Cross-Modal Representation Alignment
notes.scope: Orients the domain: how images, audio, and text get mapped into a common or fused representation, and the taxonomy of ways systems combine modalities. IN: the shared-embedding vs fuse-into-LM paradigms, fusion taxonomy (early/late/cross-attention/projector), why a shared space enables zero-shot transfer. OUT: the contrastive loss math (link CLIP note), specific VLM wiring (link VLM Architectures), diffusion conditioning (link Classifier-Free Guidance).
key_points: The core problem: modalities differ in dimensionality, statistics, and token count; a model must project them into a common space where attention can operate across them

Two dominant paradigms: contrastive alignment into a shared metric space (CLIP-style dual encoders; best for retrieval/classification) vs fusion into a generative LM (VLMs; best for open-ended generation)

Fusion taxonomy with tradeoffs: early/pixel fusion (Fuyu — patches straight in), late fusion (separate encoders joined at the end), intermediate via cross-attention (Flamingo), via projector into the token stream (LLaVA); axes = param count, whether the LLM stays frozen, flexibility
Alignment is not identity: even trained shared spaces retain a modality gap where image and text embeddings occupy separate regions (forward-ref)
Why a shared space gives zero-shot: classification becomes 'which text embedding is nearest,' so a new class needs only a prompt, no retraining
Failure mode: naive concatenation of raw features without alignment training yields modality collapse — the 'blind' VLM that answers from text priors and ignores the image
links: Concept - CLIP and Contrastive Vision-Language Training
Concept - The Modality Gap in Contrastive Models

notes.title: Concept - Vision Transformers
notes.scope: How a transformer processes images by tokenizing them into patches. IN: patchify + linear projection, [CLS] token vs pooling, learned position embeddings and interpolation, ViT-B/L/H config numerology, the data-hunger tradeoff vs CNNs, DeiT distillation, self-supervised ViTs (MAE/DINOv2). OUT: the attention math itself (link Attention Mechanism), contrastive training (link CLIP), arbitrary resolution (link Any-Resolution Vision Encoding).
key_points: Patchify: split image into non-overlapping P*P patches (P=16 typical, 224/16 -> 14x14 = 196 tokens), flatten each to 3P^2 values, linear-project to d; this is literally a strided conv with kernel=stride=P
Position: ViT uses learned 1D position embeddings (not RoPE); running at a new resolution needs 2D bicubic interpolation of the position grid — a common quiet source of degradation
[CLS] token vs mean-pooling: original ViT prepends a class token whose attention becomes a saliency map (attention rollout); many later models mean-pool instead

Data hunger: ViT-B underperforms ResNets below ~100M images (JFT-300M was the unlock, Dosovitskiy et al. 2021); DeiT (Touvron 2021) recovered ImageNet-only training via distillation from a CNN teacher plus heavy augmentation
Config numerology: ViT-B/16 = 12 layers, d=768, 12 heads, 86M params; ViT-L/14 = 304M; head-dim 64; halving patch size = 4x tokens = 16x attention FLOPs

Failure modes: quadratic cost in patch count; position-embedding interpolation artifacts at off-training resolutions; high-norm outlier tokens dumped in background patches that corrupt attention maps (forward-ref registers)
Self-supervised ViT features: MAE (He 2022) masked-patch reconstruction; DINO/DINOv2 (Caron 2021, Oquab 2023) yield strong dense features widely reused as VLM/generation encoders
links: Concept - Register Tokens and ViT Attention Artifacts
Concept - CLIP and Contrastive Vision-Language Training
Concept - Matrix Multiplication as the Atom of Deep Learning

notes.title: Concept - CLIP and Contrastive Vision-Language Training
notes.scope: Contrastive image-text pretraining that yields a shared embedding space usable zero-shot. IN: dual-encoder architecture, symmetric InfoNCE, learned temperature, in-batch-negative scaling, zero-shot classification via prompts, prompt ensembling, data curation (WIT/LAION/DataComp). OUT: the sigmoid variant (link SigLIP), the modality gap (link Modality Gap), using CLIP inside a VLM (link Vision-Language Connectors).
key_points: Architecture: image encoder (ViT or ResNet) + text encoder (transformer), each projecting to a shared d-dim space; L2-normalize; compare by cosine similarity

Loss: symmetric InfoNCE over the N x N in-batch similarity matrix — softmax rows (image->text) and columns (text->image), cross-entropy against the diagonal; learned temperature tau (init 0.07, clamped) scales logits
Negatives are the other in-batch pairs, so quality scales with batch size (CLIP used 32,768); this coupling to a global batch is the central scaling pain that motivates SigLIP
Data: 400M image-text pairs (WIT); caption supervision is noisy but scale makes it work; DataComp/LAION showed data curation beats architecture for CLIP quality
Zero-shot: embed 'a photo of a {class}' per label and take max cosine; prompt templates + 80-prompt ensembling adds several ImageNet points; CLIP ViT-L/14 hits ~75% zero-shot ImageNet top-1

Failure modes: bag-of-words behavior / weak compositionality ('red cube on blue sphere'), poor counting/OCR/spatial relations, prompt-wording sensitivity, brittleness of the 'a photo of' template under distribution shift
Downstream reuse: the default VLM vision tower for years; its text encoder also conditions Stable Diffusion
links: Concept - SigLIP and the Sigmoid Contrastive Loss
Concept - The Modality Gap in Contrastive Models

notes.title: Concept - SigLIP and the Sigmoid Contrastive Loss
notes.scope: The sigmoid pairwise loss that replaced softmax InfoNCE and became the default VLM vision tower. IN: sigmoid loss math, why it decouples from the global batch, the learnable bias term, chunked peer-to-peer negatives, SigLIP/SigLIP2 results and adoption. OUT: the general contrastive framing (link CLIP), encoder selection tradeoffs (link Decision - Choosing a Vision Encoder).
key_points: Softmax InfoNCE needs a normalization over all negatives -> the full N x N matrix and a global all-gather across data-parallel ranks; sigmoid loss (Zhai et al. 2023, SigLIP) treats every image-text pair as an independent binary classification (positive on the diagonal, negative off) summing per-pair sigmoid BCE

Because the loss decomposes per pair, you can shard the batch, compute local blocks, and swap negatives peer-to-peer with a small all-gather — trains well at small batch and scales to huge batch without the softmax memory blowup
Learnable bias b is initialized strongly negative (e.g., -10) to counter the extreme negative:positive imbalance early in training when almost every pair is a negative
Results: SigLIP matches or beats CLIP at far smaller batch (e.g., 16k); SigLIP-So400m (shape-optimized, 400M) is a workhorse; SigLIP2 (2025) adds captioning and self-distillation objectives
Adoption: SigLIP-So400m at 384-448px is the vision tower in PaliGemma, Idefics2/3, and many 2024-25 open VLMs — strong features at higher resolution than CLIP-336
Nuance/failure: less batch-sensitive but still benefits from scale; the bias/temperature interaction needs care; inherits CLIP's weak compositionality
links: Concept - CLIP and Contrastive Vision-Language Training
Decision - Choosing a Vision Encoder for a VLM

notes.title: Concept - The Modality Gap in Contrastive Models
notes.scope: The empirical phenomenon that image and text embeddings in CLIP-like models occupy separate, non-overlapping cones of the shared space despite the contrastive objective. IN: the cone effect, gap-at-initialization, why contrastive loss preserves it, temperature's role, implications for retrieval and cross-modal arithmetic. OUT: the base contrastive training (link CLIP).
key_points: Liang et al. 2022 ('Mind the Gap'): plot CLIP image vs text embeddings and they form two distinct cones; the mean image embedding and mean text embedding stay separated by a consistent offset even after training

Origin — the cone effect: deep nets at random init map inputs into a narrow cone, and two different encoders (image vs text) land in different cones; contrastive loss only needs the relative ordering (matched pair closer than mismatched), so it satisfies the objective while leaving a global offset intact
Temperature matters: low tau makes the loss focus on the hardest negatives, which does not pull the two modalities together globally, so the gap persists
You can shrink the gap by shifting one modality's embeddings, and this sometimes improves zero-shot accuracy and fairness metrics — evidence the gap is partly a nuisance artifact, not signal

Implications: cross-modal cosine similarities are not directly comparable to within-modal ones; naive 'image + (text_A - text_B)' arithmetic is unreliable; retrieval thresholds must be modality-aware; a VLM projector must learn to bridge this gap, not merely resize
Related framing: alignment/uniformity tradeoff (Wang & Isola 2020); helps explain why feeding raw CLIP features into an LLM underperforms a learned projection
links: Concept - CLIP and Contrastive Vision-Language Training
Concept - SigLIP and the Sigmoid Contrastive Loss

notes.title: Concept - Register Tokens and ViT Attention Artifacts
notes.scope: The discovery that ViTs stash high-norm outlier tokens in low-information background patches, corrupting attention maps and dense features, and the register-token fix. IN: the artifact phenomenon, high-norm 'massive activation' tokens, why they emerge, register tokens as fix, impact on DINOv2/dense prediction/interpretability. OUT: ViT fundamentals (link Vision Transformers).
key_points: Darcet et al. 2023 ('Vision Transformers Need Registers'): attention maps of trained ViTs (supervised, CLIP, DINO) show a few patches in uniform background regions with anomalously high activation norm (~10x typical), producing noisy uninterpretable attention

Mechanism: the model recycles patches it deems low-information as storage for global image-level features (a computation scratchpad), overwriting local content — visible as norm spikes and hurting dense tasks (segmentation, depth) that need clean per-patch features

Fix: append a handful (4) of learnable 'register' tokens to the input, discarded at output; they give the model dedicated scratchpad slots, cleaning attention maps and improving dense downstream performance and interpretability
DINOv2 adopted registers; the phenomenon parallels attention sinks in LLMs and 'massive activations' (Sun et al. 2024) — both are somewhere to dump attention mass

Practical impact: if you build a VLM on raw ViT patch features, these outlier tokens inject noise into the LLM; interpretability of vision features must account for them; explains why some CLIP attention visualizations look broken
Non-obvious: this is the vision analog of the register/attention-sink story from StreamingLLM — a cross-modal recurrence of the same mechanism
links: Concept - The Modality Gap in Contrastive Models

notes.title: Concept - VLM Architectures
notes.scope: The taxonomy and wiring of vision-language models that feed images into an LLM. IN: the three families (cross-attention/Flamingo, projector/LLaVA, early-fusion/native), where the vision encoder sits, frozen vs trained components, image-token budget, single vs interleaved multi-image. OUT: projector internals (link Connectors), specific systems (link LLaVA/Flamingo breakdowns), native depth (link Native and Any-to-Any), resolution handling (link Any-Resolution).
key_points: Family A — cross-attention (Flamingo, Llama-3.2-Vision): vision features enter through added gated cross-attention layers interleaved in a frozen LLM; keeps LLM weights intact and scales to many images but adds params and complexity

Family B — projector/prefix (LLaVA, Qwen-VL, InternVL, most open VLMs): vision encoder -> connector (MLP/resampler) -> image tokens prepended into the LLM token stream as soft prompts; simplest and most popular; the LLM must be (partly) trained

Family C — early/native fusion (Fuyu, Chameleon, Gemini): no separate pretrained vision encoder; image patches linearly projected as tokens from scratch, or images tokenized to discrete codes; one transformer over mixed modalities

Key design axes: frozen vs unfrozen encoder/LLM; image-token count (one 336px CLIP image ~ 576 tokens, multi-tile can be thousands); whether image tokens attend bidirectionally within the image or causally; single vs interleaved multi-image/video
Training recipe (LLaVA-style): stage 1 aligns the projector on caption data (freeze encoder + LLM), stage 2 instruction-tunes (unfreeze LLM); stage-2 SFT data quality dominates final quality
Failure modes: the 'blind' VLM answering from language priors, OCR/small-text failure at low resolution, token-budget blowup killing context and latency, object/attribute hallucination
links: Concept - Native and Any-to-Any Multimodal Models

notes.title: Concept - Vision-Language Connectors
notes.scope: The module that maps vision-encoder features into the LLM token space in projector-style VLMs. IN: linear vs MLP projector, Q-Former (BLIP-2), Perceiver resampler, pixel-shuffle/unshuffle token reduction, the token-count vs quality tradeoff, feature-layer choice. OUT: cross-attention fusion (link Flamingo), the encoder itself (link ViT/SigLIP).
key_points: Simplest: a linear or 2-layer MLP projecting each patch feature to LLM d; LLaVA-1.5 switched linear -> MLP for a measurable bump; keeps one token per patch (576 for 336px)

Query-based resamplers: BLIP-2's Q-Former uses ~32 learned queries cross-attending to vision features to compress to 32 tokens but is hard to train and can bottleneck fine detail; Flamingo/Idefics Perceiver resampler is similar

Token reduction: pixel-shuffle/unshuffle (InternVL) merges a 2x2 patch neighborhood into one token (4x fewer tokens, restores channels); Qwen2-VL uses an MLP merger on 2x2 blocks — the main lever on the token-budget problem

Tradeoff: fewer tokens = cheaper LLM and more context room but lost OCR/fine detail; more tokens = better perception but worse latency and context pressure; resamplers empirically lose more detail than pixel-shuffle at the same token count
The connector must bridge the modality gap and the encoder-vs-LLM distribution mismatch — a nontrivial learned map, not a resize
Failure modes: an undertrained projector yields weak grounding; over-aggressive compression causes OCR collapse; feature-layer choice matters (LLaVA uses the penultimate ViT layer, not the last)
links: Concept - The Modality Gap in Contrastive Models

notes.title: Concept - Any-Resolution Vision Encoding
notes.scope: Techniques for feeding images of arbitrary size and aspect ratio to a ViT trained at fixed resolution. IN: AnyRes tiling (LLaVA-NeXT), dynamic tiling (InternVL), NaViT patch-n-pack, Qwen2-VL native dynamic resolution with 2D/M-RoPE, position-embedding interpolation, token-budget math. OUT: base ViT (link Vision Transformers), connector token reduction (link Connectors).
key_points: Problem: CLIP/SigLIP ViTs are trained at 224-448px, but real images are high-res and varied aspect ratio; downsampling to 336 destroys small text and detail (OCR fails)

AnyRes/tiling (LLaVA-NeXT, InternVL): split the image into a grid of native-resolution tiles, encode each separately, add a downsized global thumbnail, concatenate tokens — e.g., 4 tiles + thumbnail = 5x576 ~ 2880 tokens for one image, which is why VLM context and latency blow up
Position-embedding interpolation: to run a fixed-grid ViT at higher res you bicubically interpolate the learned position grid; it works but degrades, which 2D-RoPE avoids

NaViT (Dehghani et al. 2023) 'patch n' pack': pack variable-resolution images into one sequence with masked attention (no padding waste) and factorized position embeddings — native aspect ratios and a large training-efficiency win

Qwen2-VL: native dynamic resolution with multimodal 2D rotary embeddings (M-RoPE), variable token count per image, unified image/video handling — a modern default; InternVL dynamic tiling picks an aspect-ratio-matched tile layout
Failure modes: tiling seams split text/objects across tiles (grounding errors); token budget explodes and starves the text context; aspect-ratio bucketing choices bias which images degrade

notes.title: Breakdown - LLaVA
notes.scope: The canonical open projector-style VLM and the training recipe that made it reproducible. IN: CLIP ViT-L + MLP + Vicuna wiring, two-stage training, GPT-4-generated visual instruction data, LLaVA-1.5/NeXT changes, exact configs and numbers. OUT: general VLM taxonomy (link VLM Architectures), connector variants (link Connectors).
key_points: Architecture (Liu et al. 2023): frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 penultimate-layer features (576 tokens at 336px) -> projector -> Vicuna-7B/13B; original used a single linear layer, LLaVA-1.5 upgraded to a 2-layer MLP and 336px encoder

Data innovation: 'visual instruction tuning' — used text-only GPT-4 to synthesize multimodal instruction data from COCO captions and boxes (conversation, detailed description, complex reasoning), ~158K samples; this distillation trick is the real contribution

Two stages: (1) feature alignment — freeze encoder + LLM, train only the projector on 558K caption pairs; (2) end-to-end instruction tuning — unfreeze the LLM (keep encoder frozen), train on the 158K plus academic-task data; ~1 day on 8xA100 for 7B
LLaVA-1.5 result: SOTA on many VQA benchmarks with only ~1.2M total samples of public data — showed you do not need Flamingo-scale data
LLaVA-NeXT (1.6): AnyRes tiling for higher effective resolution, better OCR/reasoning, more SFT data
What is dated/wrong: frozen CLIP caps OCR and fine detail; 576-token images; weak grounding/counting; hallucination driven by strong LLM priors; benchmark-contamination concerns
What to steal: freeze-then-unfreeze staging, distilling instruction data from a stronger model, the MLP connector, penultimate-layer features
links: Concept - CLIP and Contrastive Vision-Language Training
Playbook - Training a VLM from a Vision Encoder and an LLM

notes.title: Breakdown - Flamingo
notes.scope: DeepMind's cross-attention VLM that set the interleaved few-shot multimodal template. IN: Perceiver resampler, gated cross-attention with tanh gating, frozen encoder + frozen Chinchilla LLM, interleaved image-text training, in-context few-shot multimodality. OUT: projector-style VLMs (link LLaVA), the resampler as a connector (link Connectors).
key_points: Alayrac et al. 2022: freeze a pretrained vision encoder (NFNet) and a frozen Chinchilla LLM, then insert trainable GATED XATTN-DENSE layers between LLM blocks that cross-attend to visual features; only the new layers and the resampler train
Perceiver Resampler: maps a variable number of vision features to a fixed 64 visual tokens via learned latent queries, decoupling image resolution/count from LLM cost

tanh gating: cross-attention output is multiplied by tanh(alpha) with alpha initialized to 0, so at init the model is exactly the original LLM and the gates open during training — the stability trick that lets you graft modules onto a frozen LLM without wrecking it

Interleaved training on M3W (webpages with inline images) plus image-text pairs enables few-shot: show a few (image, answer) examples in context, then a new image; this in-context multimodal ability was the headline
Per-image causal masking: each text token attends only to the immediately preceding image, keeping interleaved sequences coherent
What is dated: NFNet encoder, no high-res/OCR focus; projector-style (LLaVA) became more popular for simplicity, but cross-attention returned in Llama-3.2-Vision precisely to keep the LLM frozen
What to steal: zero-init gating for grafting modules, the resampler for a fixed token budget, interleaved data for multi-image/few-shot
links: Concept - Chain-of-Thought and Why It Works
Concept - Native and Any-to-Any Multimodal Models

notes.title: Concept - Native and Any-to-Any Multimodal Models
notes.scope: Models that process and/or generate multiple modalities in one transformer without a bolted-on encoder. IN: early-fusion input (Fuyu, Chameleon), discrete multimodal tokenization, mixed-modal training instability and the norm fixes, unified generation (Chameleon output, Transfusion, GPT-4o), diffusion+AR hybrids. OUT: projector VLMs (link VLM Architectures), image-token internals (link VQ-VAE), diffusion internals (link Diffusion Models).
key_points: Fuyu (Adept 2023): no vision encoder — image patches are linearly projected straight into a decoder-only LLM as tokens; radically simple and handles arbitrary resolution naturally

Chameleon (Meta 2024): early-fusion, tokenizes images to discrete VQ codes and interleaves them with text in one vocabulary, trained mixed-modal from scratch and able to output image tokens; reported serious training instabilities requiring QK-Norm and norm reordering to keep logits stable across modalities (the load-bearing tribal detail)

Transfusion (Meta 2024): a single transformer trained with LM cross-entropy on text tokens AND a diffusion loss on continuous image patches simultaneously — combines AR text with diffusion images and avoids the fidelity loss of VQ tokenization
GPT-4o / Gemini: natively multimodal, trained on interleaved modalities end-to-end; 4o does image and audio in and out at low latency (folklore: discrete audio tokens for realtime)

Core tension: discrete tokenization (VQ) unifies the objective but loses visual fidelity, while continuous + diffusion preserves fidelity but complicates the single-loss story — any-to-any is where this is actively fought out

Failure modes: modality competition (one loss dominates, the other modality is undertrained), logit-scale divergence across modalities needing norm tricks, a much larger vocabulary, and hard-to-design evaluation
links: Concept - VQ-VAE and Discrete Visual Tokenization
Concept - Neural Audio Codecs and Residual Vector Quantization

notes.title: Gotchas - Vision-Language Models
notes.scope: Aggregated pitfalls when building, training, and serving VLMs, ordered by pain. OUT: diffusion-side pitfalls (link Gotchas - Diffusion Training and Sampling); eval methodology (link Evaluation notes).
key_points: The blind VLM: model answers from language priors and ignores the image; detect with a counterfactual image-swap test; caused by weak alignment, too-strong LLM prior, or text-heavy SFT
Image-token budget blowup: AnyRes tiling produces thousands of tokens per image -> context overflow, slow prefill, and cost; symptom is truncated context and latency spikes
OCR/small-text failure at low resolution: 336px cannot read fine text; fix is higher resolution or tiling, but watch the token cost

Image-placeholder / chat-template mismatch: the number of <image> placeholder tokens must equal the projector's output token count, and the train vs inference template must match, or quality silently collapses
Object/attribute hallucination: names plausible-but-absent objects (POPE benchmark); worsened by strong LLM priors and by SFT data that describes prototypical scenes
Masking/padding bugs with multi-image batches: image tokens given a causal mask when they should be bidirectional; left-padding errors across a batch of different image counts
Frozen-encoder ceiling: CLIP features cap fine-grained perception no matter how much you SFT the LLM
Multi-image/video generalization: models trained on single images degrade on many images and lose temporal ordering; and eval is contamination- and prompt-format-sensitive (route to Evaluation)

notes.title: Decision - Choosing a Vision Encoder for a VLM
notes.scope: How to pick the vision tower for a VLM. IN: CLIP vs SigLIP vs DINOv2 vs combined (RADIO/feature fusion), resolution vs token budget, which feature layer, frozen vs tuned encoder. OUT: encoder internals (link ViT/CLIP/SigLIP), the connector (link Vision-Language Connectors).
key_points: Default (as of 2025): SigLIP-So400m at 384-448px — strong language-aligned features, good OCR at higher resolution, efficient; this is the modern workhorse
CLIP ViT-L/14-336: the legacy default (LLaVA) — fine but weaker than SigLIP at comparable scale

DINOv2: best pure-vision dense/spatial features (segmentation, depth, grounding) but not language-aligned, so worse for VQA alone; combine with CLIP/SigLIP (Cambrian-1's spatial-vision aggregator, or RADIO distilling multiple teachers) for grounding-heavy tasks
Resolution vs token budget is the central tradeoff: higher res / tiling improves OCR and detail but multiplies tokens (see Any-Resolution), pressuring context and latency
Which layer: penultimate-layer features usually beat the last (the last is over-specialized to the contrastive objective) — the LLaVA finding
Frozen vs tuned encoder: freeze for stability and data efficiency; only unfreeze with an LR warmup and lots of data, at risk of catastrophic forgetting in the encoder
Decision flippers: OCR/document tasks -> high-res SigLIP or a doc-specialized encoder; grounding/robotics -> add DINOv2; tight latency/context -> aggressive token reduction and a smaller encoder
links: Concept - CLIP and Contrastive Vision-Language Training
Concept - SigLIP and the Sigmoid Contrastive Loss

notes.title: Playbook - Training a VLM from a Vision Encoder and an LLM
notes.scope: End-to-end procedure to build a projector-style VLM from an off-the-shelf encoder plus LLM. IN: component selection, the two-stage recipe, data mix, freezing schedule, hyperparameters, verification probes. OUT: pretraining the base LLM (link Anatomy of a Pretraining Run), training the encoder (link CLIP/SigLIP).
key_points: Select components: encoder (SigLIP/CLIP) + LLM (Qwen/Llama) + connector (MLP or pixel-shuffle); decide target resolution and token budget up front

Stage 1 alignment: freeze encoder + LLM, train only the connector on ~0.5-1M caption/interleaved pairs; expected observation = alignment loss drops steadily; deviation = a high plateau means projector LR too low or a feature-layer mismatch
Wire-check: choose the penultimate feature layer and verify image-token count equals the number of <image> placeholders in the chat template before any long run

Stage 2 instruction tuning: unfreeze the LLM (keep encoder frozen unless you have abundant data), SFT on high-quality multimodal instructions mixed with some text-only data to prevent language regression; LR ~2e-5 for the LLM, higher for the connector, ~1 epoch
Resolution: enable AnyRes tiling if OCR is needed and budget the resulting tokens against context and latency
Verify: run VQA + OCR + hallucination (POPE) probes and a counterfactual image-swap test to confirm the model actually uses the image

When it goes wrong: blind model -> better SFT data / check masking / raise image-token weight; OCR fails -> raise resolution; language skills regressed -> add text-only replay; loss NaN -> check bf16 and encoder-output normalization
links: Decision - Choosing a Vision Encoder for a VLM

notes.title: Reference - Vision Encoders and Multimodal Models
notes.scope: Front-loaded lookup tables for vision encoders, VLMs, image/video generators, and audio models with specs, plus the token-count and latent-scaling formulas. OUT: mechanism explanations (link the concept notes).
key_points: Vision encoders table: CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (304M, 576 tokens), SigLIP-So400m/384 (400M), DINOv2-L, EVA-CLIP — columns for params, native resolution, token count, objective, license

notes.title: Deep Dive - Diffusion Models
notes.scope: The full diffusion framework from DDPM math to sampling. IN: forward noising, reverse denoising, the simple loss, epsilon/v/x0 parameterizations, the score-matching connection, DDPM/DDIM, noise schedules and SNR, the SDE/ODE view. OUT: latent-space diffusion (link Latent Diffusion), guidance (link Classifier-Free Guidance), sampler depth (link Samplers), the flow-matching generalization (link Flow Matching), the DiT backbone (link Diffusion Transformers).
key_points: Forward process: q(x_t|x_0) = N(sqrt(a_bar_t) x_0, (1 - a_bar_t) I) with a closed form to jump to any t; x_t = sqrt(a_bar_t) x_0 + sqrt(1 - a_bar_t) * epsilon, schedule beta_t giving a_bar_t

Reverse process: learn epsilon_theta(x_t, t) to predict the noise; the ELBO simplifies (Ho et al. 2020, DDPM) to L_simple = E || epsilon - epsilon_theta(x_t, t) ||^2, a denoising objective that drops the ELBO weighting and trains better

Score connection (Song & Ermon 2019/2021): epsilon-prediction is equivalent to estimating the score grad_x log p(x_t) up to scaling; diffusion is a discretized SDE, which is what enables deterministic ODE samplers

Parameterizations: epsilon-pred (standard), x0-pred, and v-pred (Salimans & Ho 2022, better at high noise and for distillation and zero-SNR); plus loss weighting choices like min-SNR-gamma (Hang 2023)
Sampling: ancestral DDPM (~1000 steps, slow) vs DDIM (Song 2021) deterministic non-Markovian at 20-50 steps; classifier-free guidance layers on top
Noise schedules: linear (DDPM), cosine (Nichol & Dhariwal 2021, better for small images), and the zero-terminal-SNR fix (forward-ref gotchas)

Architecture walkthrough (required): sinusoidal time embedding -> MLP, U-Net with residual blocks and self/cross-attention at low resolution, conditioning injection; include the forward+reverse diagram

Evolution (required): score matching -> DDPM -> DDIM -> latent diffusion -> classifier-free guidance -> v-pred/EDM (Karras 2022) -> flow matching/rectified flow -> DiT; note what flow matching replaces
Failure modes: too few steps = blur/artifacts; schedule/parameterization mismatch; exposure bias (train on real x_t, sample on estimates) compounds error
links: Snippet - DDPM Training and Sampling Loop

notes.title: Concept - Latent Diffusion
notes.scope: Running diffusion in a compressed VAE latent space instead of pixels — the Stable Diffusion architecture pattern. IN: the perceptual autoencoder, why latent (compute), cross-attention text conditioning, latent channels and the scaling constant, the two-stage train. OUT: DDPM math (link Diffusion Models), the specific SD family and history (link Stable Diffusion breakdown), samplers (link Samplers).
key_points: Rombach et al. 2022 (LDM): train an autoencoder to compress images 8x (512x512x3 -> 64x64x4 latent), then run diffusion in that latent — ~48x fewer spatial elements makes training and inference tractable on consumer GPUs
The autoencoder is perceptual + adversarial (LPIPS loss + patch-GAN discriminator), not pixel-MSE, so latents preserve perceptual detail; comes in KL-regularized or VQ-regularized variants
Conditioning: text enters via cross-attention — CLIP/T5 text embeddings act as keys/values in the U-Net's cross-attention layers, which is how the prompt steers denoising

Latent scaling factor: latents are multiplied by a constant (SD 0.18215) so their variance is ~1 for the diffusion model — a magic number that silently breaks output if forgotten (forward-ref gotchas)
Why it dominated: it made open text-to-image feasible; essentially all image diffusion (SD/SDXL/SD3/FLUX) is latent diffusion

Failure modes: the VAE is the fidelity ceiling — fine text, faces, and hands are lost in the 8x compression; VAE decode artifacts (grid patterns, color shift); 4-channel latents limited detail, which is why SD3/FLUX moved to 16-channel latents
links: Concept - VQ-VAE and Discrete Visual Tokenization
Concept - CLIP and Contrastive Vision-Language Training

notes.title: Concept - Classifier-Free Guidance
notes.scope: The technique that trades diversity for prompt adherence in conditional diffusion. IN: joint conditional/unconditional training, the guidance extrapolation formula and scale, oversaturation at high scale and its fixes (dynamic thresholding, rescaling, limited-interval guidance), negative prompts. OUT: DDPM basics (link Diffusion Models), classifier-guidance history (mention only).
key_points: Ho & Salimans 2022: train one model for both conditional epsilon_theta(x, c) and unconditional epsilon_theta(x, empty) by dropping the condition ~10% of the time; at sampling, extrapolate eps_hat = eps_uncond + w * (eps_cond - eps_uncond) with guidance weight w
Mechanism: pushes samples toward regions where the conditional is more likely than the unconditional, sharpening prompt adherence at the cost of diversity and mode coverage
Typical w: ~7.5 for SD, ~3-5 for SDXL; w=1 means no guidance; w>15 tends to oversaturate with blown highlights and artifacts

Oversaturation fixes: dynamic thresholding (Imagen, Saharia 2022) clamps the predicted x0 by percentile; guidance rescaling (Lin et al. 2023) rescales to match std; limited-interval guidance (Kynkaanniemi et al. 2024) applies CFG only in a middle-noise window for a large quality gain; also CFG++/APG
Replaced classifier guidance (Dhariwal & Nichol 2021), which needed a separate noise-robust classifier; CFG needs none
Negative prompts: swap the unconditional branch for an embedded negative prompt to steer away from it — purely an inference-time trick
Failure modes: high w -> oversaturation and reduced diversity ('deep-fried' look); guidance interacts with sampler and step count; few-step distilled models (LCM/Turbo) fold guidance into the weights

notes.title: Concept - Flow Matching
notes.scope: The continuous-time generative framework (conditional flow matching / rectified flow) that underlies SD3, FLUX, and modern generators. IN: the CNF/ODE view, the conditional flow-matching objective, optimal-transport/rectified straight paths, velocity prediction, the relation to diffusion, few-step sampling. OUT: DDPM specifics (link Diffusion Models), the DiT backbone (link Diffusion Transformers).
key_points: Idea (Lipman et al. 2022, CFM; Liu et al. 2022, rectified flow): learn a velocity field v_theta(x, t) that transports noise x_1 ~ N(0, I) to data x_0 along a probability path, then sample by solving the ODE dx/dt = v_theta

Conditional flow matching: regress v_theta against the conditional velocity of a simple per-sample path; with the linear/OT path x_t = (1-t) x_0 + t x_1 the target velocity is just (x_1 - x_0) — a dead-simple regression with no noise-schedule bookkeeping
Rectified flow: straight-line paths make the ODE easy to integrate in few steps; a 'reflow' procedure straightens trajectories further toward 1-2 step generation
Relation to diffusion: diffusion is a curved-path special case; flow matching generalizes it, typically giving straighter paths, fewer sampling steps, and more stable training
Adoption: SD3 uses rectified flow with logit-normal timestep sampling (and a resolution-dependent shift); FLUX likewise; the velocity/v-prediction view unifies with the EDM/score formulation
Why labs switched: a simpler objective, better observed scaling, fewer steps, and clean composition with DiT/MMDiT backbones
Failure modes: ODE-solver error at very few steps; the timestep-sampling distribution (logit-normal, high-res shift) matters a lot; path choice affects sample quality
links: Concept - Matrix Multiplication as the Atom of Deep Learning

notes.title: Concept - Diffusion Samplers and Schedulers
notes.scope: The numerical solvers and noise schedules that turn a trained diffusion/flow model into images in N steps. IN: DDPM/DDIM, DPM-Solver(++), Euler/Heun ancestral, Karras sigmas, step-count economics, ODE vs SDE, few-step distillation (LCM/Turbo/consistency). OUT: model training (link Diffusion Models), guidance (link Classifier-Free Guidance).
key_points: Two families: stochastic samplers (ancestral, add noise each step — more diverse, need more steps) vs deterministic ODE samplers (DDIM, DPM-Solver, Euler — fewer steps, reproducible)

DDIM (Song 2021): non-Markovian deterministic, 20-50 steps; DPM-Solver / DPM-Solver++ (Lu et al. 2022): high-order ODE solvers giving good images in 10-20 steps, with ++ handling guidance and latent models better
Karras et al. 2022 (EDM): reframes the schedule as noise levels sigma; the 'Karras sigma' spacing improves low-step quality, paired with the 2nd-order Heun sampler
Step-count economics: quality saturates (SDXL is good at ~30 DPM++ steps); each step is one full backbone forward, and with CFG it is two forwards, so steps x 2 drives latency (route to serving)
Few-step distillation: LCM / LCM-LoRA (consistency distillation), SDXL-Turbo / ADD (adversarial diffusion distillation), and flow reflow reach 1-4 steps by folding guidance in

The scheduler must match training: v-pred vs epsilon-pred, and zero-terminal-SNR training requires a matching sampler and trailing-timestep selection or you get washed-out/dark images (route to gotchas)
Failure modes: too few steps = blur/artifacts; wrong sampler for the parameterization; ancestral noise at low steps = grain

notes.title: Concept - Diffusion Transformers (DiT)
notes.scope: Replacing the diffusion U-Net with a transformer over latent patches. IN: patchify latents to tokens, adaLN-zero conditioning, clean scaling behavior, MMDiT dual-stream (SD3), Sora/FLUX usage, the attention-cost problem. OUT: DDPM math (link Diffusion Models), the flow-matching objective (link Flow Matching), video specifics (link Video Generation).
key_points: Peebles & Xie 2023 (DiT): operate on latent patches as tokens through a plain transformer and show diffusion quality scales cleanly with transformer FLOPs (more Gflops -> lower FID) — the 'scaling laws for diffusion' moment

adaLN-zero conditioning: inject timestep + class/text via adaptive LayerNorm whose scale/shift/gate are predicted by an MLP from the conditioning, with the residual gate zero-initialized (same idea as Flamingo gating) — the key stability trick
MMDiT (SD3, Esser et al. 2024): separate weight streams for text and image tokens that attend jointly, giving much better text rendering and prompt adherence than cross-attention-only U-Nets

Why it won: U-Nets do not scale as gracefully, and transformers reuse all LLM infrastructure (FlashAttention, tensor/pipeline parallelism, better hardware utilization); FLUX, SD3, Sora, and PixArt are all DiT-based
Cost: attention is quadratic in token count, so high-res and video are expensive — this motivates latent compression and windowed/spatiotemporal attention
Failure modes: needs the zero-init gate for stable training; high-res token blowup; the 2D/3D positional encoding for patches must be chosen carefully (RoPE-2D/3D)

notes.title: Concept - ControlNet and Spatial Conditioning for Diffusion
notes.scope: Adding spatial/structural control (edges, pose, depth) and image prompts to a pretrained diffusion model. IN: ControlNet trainable-copy + zero-convolution mechanism, T2I-Adapter, IP-Adapter (image prompt), how the base model stays intact, composition. OUT: text conditioning/CFG (link Latent Diffusion/CFG), LoRA fine-tuning (link LoRA).
key_points: ControlNet (Zhang et al. 2023): clone the U-Net encoder into a trainable copy, feed it the control image (Canny/depth/pose), and inject its outputs into the frozen base via zero-initialized 1x1 convolutions ('zero convs')

Zero-conv trick: initialized to zero so at step 0 the ControlNet contributes nothing, leaving the base model unharmed and training stable; the connection grows as it learns — the same zero-init-gate idea as Flamingo and DiT
Keeps the large base frozen, so you train only the copy on modest per-condition data; the community produced many ControlNets (pose/depth/scribble/segmentation)

Alternatives: T2I-Adapter is a small side network (cheaper); IP-Adapter uses decoupled cross-attention for image prompts, treating a reference image as a soft condition — the basis of style/face transfer
Composition: multi-ControlNet stacking with per-condition scales; used heavily in production pipelines (product shots, pose-consistent characters)

Failure modes: control-vs-prompt conflict and leakage; zero-conv means early training looks like nothing is happening; over-strong conditioning overrides the prompt; control/latent resolution mismatch

notes.title: Breakdown - Stable Diffusion
notes.scope: The Stable Diffusion model family as an engineered system across versions. IN: SD1.5/2/SDXL/SD3 components and exact specs, VAE, text encoders, U-Net vs MMDiT, refiner, conditioning embeddings, FLUX as the successor. OUT: the latent-diffusion concept (link Latent Diffusion), the release war story (link Lore).
key_points: SD1.x: 860M U-Net, 4-channel 64x64 latent (8x VAE), frozen OpenAI CLIP ViT-L text encoder (77-token cap), epsilon-pred, linear schedule; trained on a LAION-2B aesthetic subset at 512px
SD2: switched to the OpenCLIP-H text encoder (which changed prompt behavior in ways users disliked), added a v-pred option, 768px

SDXL (Podell et al. 2023): 2.6B U-Net, TWO text encoders (CLIP-L + OpenCLIP-bigG concatenated), size/crop conditioning embeddings that fix SD1's cropped-subject artifacts, a separate refiner model, 1024px, latent scaling 0.13025

SD3 (Esser et al. 2024): MMDiT transformer with dual text/image streams, a rectified-flow objective, THREE text encoders (CLIP-L + CLIP-bigG + T5-XXL for legible text), and a 16-channel VAE — a large jump in typography and detail
FLUX.1 (Black Forest Labs 2024): DiT + flow matching, 12B, with guidance-distilled variants; the open SOTA as of 2025
The clever parts: latent compression, cross-attention conditioning, SDXL's size/crop conditioning, SD3's dual-stream MMDiT plus T5 for text, and 16-channel latents
What is dated/wrong: 4-channel latent detail loss, hands/text failures before SD3, the CLIP 77-token limit, and dataset/safety-filter controversies
What to steal: the VAE + conditioner + denoiser decomposition, size conditioning, and adding T5 for text rendering
links: Concept - CLIP and Contrastive Vision-Language Training
Lore - The Stable Diffusion Release and Its Aftermath

notes.title: Gotchas - Diffusion Training and Sampling
notes.scope: The arcane failure modes and folklore fixes in training and sampling diffusion models, ordered by pain. OUT: VLM-side pitfalls (link Gotchas - Vision-Language Models).
key_points: Zero terminal SNR bug (Lin et al. 2023): standard schedules never reach SNR=0 at the last timestep, so the model always sees a little signal in training but pure noise at inference — a train/test mismatch that biases outputs toward medium brightness and prevents very dark or very bright images; the fix is all four of rescale-to-zero-terminal-SNR + v-pred + trailing-timestep selection + CFG rescale together
VAE latent scaling constant (0.18215 for SD, 0.13025 for SDXL): forget it and the diffusion model sees wrong-variance latents -> garbage or washed output
CFG oversaturation at high guidance -> dynamic thresholding / guidance rescale / limited-interval guidance
Exposure bias: training conditions on ground-truth x_t but sampling conditions on model estimates, so error compounds over steps; mitigated by input perturbation during training
EMA weights: sample from the EMA copy (decay ~0.9999), not the raw training weights — forgetting this yields visibly worse samples
Aspect-ratio bucketing: square-cropping every training image teaches center bias and cropped subjects (SDXL's crop-conditioning fix); bucket by aspect ratio instead
Min-SNR loss weighting (Hang et al. 2023): unweighted L_simple over-weights easy high-SNR steps; min-SNR-gamma speeds convergence
fp16 numerics: the SDXL VAE decodes to NaNs in fp16 (needs fp32 or the fixed VAE); and a v-pred model run with an epsilon-pred sampler produces broken images

notes.title: Snippet - DDPM Training and Sampling Loop
notes.scope: A minimal runnable PyTorch DDPM: noise schedule precompute, one training step on the simple loss, and a deterministic DDIM sampling loop. OUT: the derivation and theory (link Diffusion Models).
key_points: Precompute betas (linear), alphas, and alphas_cumprod (a_bar); show the buffers a real implementation caches
q_sample: x_t = sqrt(a_bar_t) * x_0 + sqrt(1 - a_bar_t) * epsilon — the closed-form forward that lets you jump to any t in one step
Training step: sample t ~ Uniform and epsilon ~ N(0, I), predict epsilon_theta(x_t, t), take MSE against epsilon (L_simple)
Sinusoidal timestep embedding feeding a tiny MLP so the model conditions on t
DDIM deterministic sampler loop over ~50 steps: predict epsilon, estimate x0, step to x_{t-1}

Why-written-this-way notes: L_simple drops the ELBO weighting (empirically better); predict noise rather than the image; DDIM enables few-step deterministic sampling; keep the net tiny because this is didactic (real models are U-Net/DiT)
Expected output: denoises Gaussian noise into toy 2D samples; loss plateaus around 0.03-0.05

notes.title: Lore - The Stable Diffusion Release and Its Aftermath
notes.scope: The war story of open text-to-image, 2022-2024. IN: the SD1.4/1.5 open release, LAION-5B, compute/cost, the NovelAI leak, the community customization explosion, the SD3 license backlash, and the legal fallout. OUT: the architecture (link Stable Diffusion breakdown), the diffusion math (link Diffusion Models).
key_points: Aug 2022: Stability AI + CompVis + Runway release SD 1.4 open weights (1.5 later via Runway) — the first high-quality open text-to-image, trained on a LAION-2B-en aesthetic subset for ~150k A100-hours (~$600k, well-sourced folklore)
LAION-5B: the open web-scraped image-text dataset that made it possible, later pulled after Stanford found CSAM in it (2023) — the data-provenance reckoning the field inherited
Oct 2022 NovelAI leak: NAI's anime-finetuned model and hypernetwork code leaked, seeding the anime-model and hypernetwork/embedding ecosystem overnight
Ecosystem explosion: AUTOMATIC1111 webui, DreamBooth (Ruiz et al. 2022) subject fine-tuning, textual inversion, then LoRA became the dominant customization method, with Civitai as the model bazaar

Governance drama: Runway-vs-Stability tension over who released 1.5; Stability's later financial troubles; the SD3 (2024) restrictive-license backlash that pushed the community toward FLUX from ex-Stability founders (Black Forest Labs)
Legal: Getty v. Stability and Andersen v. Stability artist suits — the training-data copyright fights shaping the field

The lesson: open weights + a cheap customization method (LoRA) + a hub is an unstoppable ecosystem, and dataset provenance is a liability you inherit; evidence status = releases/lawsuits verified, cost figures well-sourced folklore, NovelAI leak details public

notes.title: Concept - VQ-VAE and Discrete Visual Tokenization
notes.scope: Turning images into discrete tokens via learned codebooks. IN: VQ-VAE quantization + commitment loss + straight-through estimator, VQGAN (perceptual+adversarial), codebook collapse and its fixes, FSQ/LFQ, why discrete tokens enable AR and any-to-any generation. OUT: continuous VAE latents (link Latent Diffusion), autoregressive/any-to-any use (link Native and Any-to-Any).
key_points: VQ-VAE (van den Oord et al. 2017): encoder -> nearest-neighbor lookup in a learned codebook of K vectors -> decoder; the token is the codebook index, and the non-differentiable argmin is handled by the straight-through estimator (copy gradients past the quantizer)
Losses: reconstruction + codebook loss || sg[z_e] - e ||^2 + commitment loss beta || z_e - sg[e] ||^2 keeping encoder outputs near the chosen codes

VQGAN (Esser et al. 2021, 'Taming Transformers'): add an LPIPS perceptual loss and a patch-GAN discriminator for sharp high-res reconstructions from a compact codebook, whose tokens then feed an autoregressive transformer

Codebook collapse (the crux, tribal knowledge): most codes go unused ('dead codes') while a few dominate, wrecking utilization; fixes are EMA codebook updates, dead-code reinit/reset, and lower-dim L2-normalized codes (improved VQGAN), plus commitment-weight tuning

Modern escape: FSQ (Mentzer et al. 2023) replaces VQ with fixed scalar quantization of a few dims (no codebook, no collapse, near-full utilization); LFQ (MagViT-2) is binary/lookup-free with a huge vocabulary — both simpler and better-utilized

Why discrete: it lets images live in one AR transformer vocabulary (Chameleon, Parti, Image GPT) and enables any-to-any, but quantization loses fidelity versus continuous latents — the core tradeoff with diffusion
Failure modes: collapse, blurry reconstruction at high compression, discriminator instability, and the vocabulary-vs-utilization tradeoff
links: Concept - Native and Any-to-Any Multimodal Models
Concept - Neural Audio Codecs and Residual Vector Quantization

notes.title: Concept - Audio Spectrograms and Mel Features
notes.scope: How audio becomes a model input. IN: waveform sampling, STFT, magnitude spectrogram, the mel filterbank, log-mel, framing (window/hop), SpecAugment, the waveform-vs-spectrogram debate. OUT: discrete neural-codec tokens (link Neural Audio Codecs), the ASR model itself (link Whisper).
key_points: Raw audio is a 1D waveform at 16kHz (speech) or 44.1-48kHz (music); 1 second = 16,000 samples — historically too long and redundant to model directly
STFT: slide a window (e.g., 25ms) with a hop (e.g., 10ms), FFT each frame -> a complex spectrogram; take magnitude -> a time x frequency 'image'; the hop sets the frame rate (10ms -> 100 frames/sec)
Mel scale: warp frequency to approximate human pitch perception (roughly linear below 1kHz, log above) via a mel filterbank; Whisper uses 80 log-mel bins (large-v3 uses 128)
Log compression: humans perceive loudness logarithmically, so log-mel compresses dynamic range and stabilizes training
SpecAugment (Park et al. 2019): mask time and frequency bands as augmentation — the standard ASR regularizer

Waveform-vs-spectrogram debate: spectrograms discard phase (needing Griffin-Lim or a neural vocoder to invert), while end-to-end waveform models (wav2vec 2.0, neural codecs) learn their own frontend — modern audio LMs use learned discrete codec tokens instead of mel (forward-ref)
Failure modes: phase loss makes reconstruction lossy; the window/hop choice trades time vs frequency resolution; a wrong sample rate silently wrecks the features
links: Concept - Neural Audio Codecs and Residual Vector Quantization
Concept - Neural Text-to-Speech and Audio Language Models

notes.title: Concept - Neural Audio Codecs and Residual Vector Quantization
notes.scope: Learned codecs that compress audio into discrete tokens for generative audio models. IN: SoundStream/EnCodec/DAC architecture, residual vector quantization (RVQ), bitrate/codebook/frame-rate math, the tokens audio LMs consume, semantic vs acoustic tokens, the multi-stream decoding problem. OUT: spectrogram features (link Spectrograms), TTS/audio-LM usage (link Neural Text-to-Speech).
key_points: SoundStream (Zeghidour et al. 2021) / EnCodec (Defossez et al. 2022) / DAC (Kumar et al. 2023): a conv encoder -> RVQ -> conv decoder trained with reconstruction + adversarial + feature-matching losses, streaming audio at 1.5-24 kbps

Residual Vector Quantization: quantize with codebook 1, take the residual, quantize with codebook 2, and so on — N_q codebooks (e.g., 8) of K=1024 entries each; more codebooks = higher fidelity/bitrate, and token rate = frame_rate x N_q (e.g., 75Hz x 8 = 600 tokens/sec)
This RVQ token stack is exactly what audio LMs model (24kHz EnCodec at ~75 frames/sec), predicting codebook indices

Semantic vs acoustic tokens (AudioLM, Borsos et al. 2022): semantic tokens (from w2v-BERT/HuBERT) capture content/prosody for long-range coherence, while acoustic tokens (from the codec RVQ) capture fidelity — a two-stage hierarchy
The multi-codebook problem: predicting N_q parallel streams needs special decoding — MusicGen's delay/interleaving pattern, VALL-E's AR-first-codebook-then-NAR-rest scheme
DAC improvements: factorized + L2-normalized codes (from improved VQGAN) reach near-100% codebook utilization at high compression
Failure modes: codebook collapse (as in VQ-VAE), the bitrate-fidelity tradeoff, awkward multi-stream decoding, and artifacts that differ between speech and music
links: Concept - VQ-VAE and Discrete Visual Tokenization

notes.title: Breakdown - Whisper
notes.scope: OpenAI's weakly-supervised multilingual ASR model. IN: the encoder-decoder transformer, log-mel input, 680k-hour weak supervision, the multitask token format, timestamps, robustness, and the hallucination-on-silence failure. OUT: spectrogram basics (link Spectrograms), the generic transformer (link The Transformer).
key_points: Radford et al. 2022: a vanilla encoder-decoder transformer; audio -> 80-channel log-mel in 30-second chunks -> conv stem -> encoder, and the decoder autoregressively emits text with special task tokens

The trick is scale + weak supervision: 680,000 hours of noisy web audio-transcript pairs (no hand labeling) across 96 languages; robustness comes from data diversity, not architecture, and it is zero-shot with no per-dataset fine-tuning

Multitask format: special tokens select the task — <|transcribe|> vs <|translate|>, a language token, and <|notimestamps|> or timestamp tokens quantized to 20ms interleaved with text; one decoder does many tasks via prompt tokens
Model sizes: tiny (39M) -> base -> small -> medium -> large-v3 (1.55B), where large-v3 uses 128 mel bins and more training data
Robustness: handles accents, noise, and jargon better than prior supervised ASR because of scale, approaching human-level on some benchmarks

Famous failure modes: hallucination on silence/non-speech (emits plausible text or repeats), repetition loops, timestamp drift, invented content during long silences, and weaker low-resource languages; 30s chunking loses long context and there is no speaker diarization
Practical fixes: VAD pre-filtering to avoid silence hallucination, faster-whisper (CTranslate2) for speed, and word-level timestamps via cross-attention alignment
links: Concept - Audio Spectrograms and Mel Features

notes.title: Concept - Neural Text-to-Speech and Audio Language Models
notes.scope: Modern speech synthesis and audio generation via codec language models and flow/diffusion. IN: codec-LM TTS (VALL-E), zero-shot voice cloning from a short prompt, AR vs NAR, flow/diffusion TTS (NaturalSpeech, E2/F5-TTS), audio LMs (AudioLM, MusicGen), and evaluation. OUT: codec token internals (link Neural Audio Codecs), spectrogram features (link Spectrograms).
key_points: Two eras: the old two-stage acoustic model (Tacotron/FastSpeech -> mel) + vocoder (WaveNet/HiFi-GAN -> waveform), versus the new codec language models operating on RVQ tokens

VALL-E (Wang et al. 2023): treat TTS as a conditional codec-token LM — condition on text plus a 3-second audio prompt and autoregressively predict EnCodec tokens, giving zero-shot voice cloning from 3s of reference; AR for the first codebook, NAR for the rest (the multi-codebook trick)

Flow/diffusion TTS: NaturalSpeech 2/3, Voicebox, and E2/F5-TTS use flow matching on continuous features for fast non-autoregressive synthesis with better stability (fewer repetition/skip errors than AR)
AudioLM (Borsos et al. 2022): a semantic-then-acoustic token hierarchy for coherent long-form audio continuation (speech and piano) without text
MusicGen (Copet et al. 2023): a single-stage codec LM for music using a codebook-delay interleaving pattern, with text and melody conditioning
Evaluation: WER (via an ASR model) for intelligibility, speaker similarity for cloning, and MOS/CMOS for quality; the deepfake/consent problem is real and drives watermarking
Failure modes: AR TTS instability (skips, repeats, babbling on hard text), flat prosody, prompt speaker leakage, hallucinated words, and long-form drift
links: Concept - Neural Audio Codecs and Residual Vector Quantization

notes.title: Concept - Video Generation
notes.scope: Generating video with diffusion/flow transformers. IN: spatiotemporal latents, the 3D/causal video VAE, spacetime patches (Sora), spatial+temporal attention factorization, temporal consistency, image-to-video, and the length/compute problem. OUT: image diffusion (link Diffusion Models), the DiT backbone (link Diffusion Transformers), the flow objective (link Flow Matching).
key_points: Core problem: video = images + time, and naive per-frame generation flickers (no temporal consistency), so motion must be modeled jointly
Early approach: add temporal attention/conv layers to a pretrained image U-Net (AnimateDiff, VideoLDM, Stable Video Diffusion) — inflate 2D to 3D and train the temporal modules on video

Sora (OpenAI 2024): a DiT over spacetime patches — a 3D VAE compresses video in space AND time into latent patches, then a diffusion transformer denoises the whole clip, with variable duration/resolution/aspect ratio via NaViT-style patch packing ('world simulator' framing)
Attention factorization: full 3D attention is O((T*H*W)^2) and infeasible, so it is factorized into spatial + temporal (or windowed) attention to control cost — still the dominant expense
3D/causal video VAE: temporal compression (e.g., 4x time, 8x space) so a clip fits in latent, made causal so clips can be extended
Modern (2024-25): flow-matching DiTs — Sora, Kling, Veo, Meta Movie Gen (flow matching), CogVideoX, Mochi — with image-to-video and keyframe conditioning; cross-shot consistency remains hard

Failure modes: temporal flicker/morphing, object-permanence failures, physics violations, hands/faces, drift over long clips, enormous compute (minutes of GPU per clip), and unsolved evaluation (VBench)
links: Concept - VQ-VAE and Discrete Visual Tokenization
